clue.text: A dry cape's inside — something supplying effective cover

parts.note: taken as written
TT, teetotal, is the crossword's usual dry

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its interior, so only the letters between the first and last are kept

parts.note: the inner letters of cape

explanation.surface: A cape that stays dry inside is good protection from the rain.
explanation.walkthrough: ATTAP (or atap) is a Malay word for thatch made from palm leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Palm-leaf thatch is a roofing material, so it is a thing that keeps the weather off a building.

clue.text: Behaviour occurring between ragtag groups

indicators.note: something occurring between the words spans their boundary, so the letters run across them

parts.note: the letters run from the end of ragtag into groups

explanation.surface: Trouble breaking out between rival gangs of ruffians.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is slang for aggressive or troublesome behaviour, so the general word covers it as a broader term.

clue.text: Ecstasy filling African people in some sacred places

indicators.note: a filling sits inside something, so the first item goes into the second

parts.note: the Temne are a people of Sierra Leone
E is the street abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drug use spreading among an African tribe at their holy sites.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMENE is the plural of temenos, a precinct set apart around an ancient Greek temple.
explanation.definitionFit: A temenos is a consecrated enclosure around a shrine, so several of them are holy precincts.

clue.text: Ingredient of summer pudding maybe concocted by ear in one go?

indicators.note: the concocted letters are placed in the attempt

parts.note: a try is one go, an attempt

indicators.note: concocted means made up, so the letters of by ear are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook throws together a summer pudding by ear, all in one attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by ear' looks like cooking without a recipe, but its letters are 'concocted' into AYBER and set 'in' TRY. The 'maybe' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Summer pudding is a British dessert of bread soaked in soft red fruit, and a tayberry, a blackberry-raspberry cross, is one possible fruit for it.

clue.text: A liberal creature associated with church mostly giving charity locally?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the creature is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
L abbreviates Liberal
'as poor as a church mouse' is the saying

explanation.surface: A generous animal linked with a church is charitable, in the local way of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locally' marks a dialect word: ALMOUS is Scots for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: Alms are gifts to the poor, which is charity; the Scots form of that word is what the clue asks for.

clue.text: Personal tag i.e. didn't get confused with city's (12, two words)

indicators.note: letters that get confused are muddled out of their order

parts.note: the letters of i.e. didn't
the letters of city's

explanation.surface: Someone's name badge got muddled up with one belonging to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: An identity disc is a small metal tag worn by a soldier to identify them, a personal label.

clue.text: Company in flying to Mars go by direction finder

indicators.note: the company abbreviation is set in among the flying letters
flying suggests letters scattered in the air, so to Mars is rearranged

parts.note: to pass is to go by

explanation.surface: A firm sends a craft flying to Mars, steered past by a direction finder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' looks like the craft's journey to Mars, but it tells you to rearrange 'to Mars'; the company abbreviation goes 'in' just before that jumble's final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An astrocompass is a navigational instrument that finds direction from the positions of the stars.

clue.text: What comes after lying in sun repeatedly? We're often baked

indicators.note: something lying in another rests inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: S for sun, twice
pud, short for pudding, is the course that follows the main one

explanation.surface: Lazing in the sun again and again, we tend to get roasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What comes after' is the dessert course, pud in British slang. Spuds are potatoes, which are often baked in their jackets.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes, called spuds informally, are commonly cooked in the oven whole, so they speak of themselves as often baked.

clue.text: Cause of disease forward fellow's turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up makes the letters read from the bottom to the top

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky, here standing for a cheeky fellow, with the 's

explanation.surface: A cheeky man's behaviour has caused an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Strep, short for streptococcus, is a bacterium that causes infections such as strep throat.

clue.text: Coconut oil product to preserve eggs soft? Reverse of that

indicators.note: the reverse of all that came before means the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it
O looks like an egg, so two eggs are OO
p, piano, is soft in music

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether coconut oil keeps eggs soft, or does the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Poonac is the oil cake left after pressing coconut kernels for oil, a by-product used as cattle feed.

clue.text: Daughter mater unexpectedly conceived

indicators.note: something happening unexpectedly is out of the expected order, so the letters of mater are rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter reveals that her mother conceived her unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: Mater is Latin, and old British school slang, for mother; here its letters are simply shuffled after D.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dreamt something is to have imagined or conceived it in the mind.

clue.text: Osteal places may afford space to this

definitions.text: Osteal places may afford space to this

parts.words: Osteal places may afford space to this
parts.note: a bony hollow, the saddle-shaped seat in the skull base, gives room to the pituitary gland

explanation.walkthrough: 'Osteal' means of bone. The clue describes the bony seat in the sphenoid bone that houses the pituitary gland.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the sella turcica is the saddle-shaped depression of the sphenoid bone in which the pituitary gland sits.

clue.text: The old set, age failing, shown the way

definitions.note: an archaic past participle meaning set or congealed; The old marks it as obsolete

indicators.note: failing means breaking down, so the letters of age fall into a new order

parts.note: led means shown the way

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned group of people, failing with age, is guided along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old set' sounds like a social clique, but it is the definition: an obsolete word meaning set, with 'The old' marking it archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Geal is an archaic verb meaning to congeal, so the past form is an old word for solidified.

clue.text: Wife entering shop and not budging once

indicators.note: one thing entering another goes inside it

parts.note: a store is a shop
w abbreviates wife

explanation.surface: A wife goes into a shop and refuses to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks an obsolete word: STOWRE is an old spelling of stour, meaning stiff or stubborn.
explanation.definitionFit: The old adjective stowre meant sturdy or stubborn, unwilling to yield or move.

clue.text: It was fired from the saddle, oil coating more than half of one

definitions.text: It was fired from the saddle

indicators.note: the oil wraps round the letters that follow, holding them inside

parts.note: petrol is an oil product, so oil stands for it

indicators.note: two of the three letters of one are kept, which is more than half of it

parts.note: taken as written, then cut to its last two letters

explanation.surface: A rider's weapon is fired, with oil coating more than half of one part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half of' one means two of its three letters; which two is settled by fitting them inside the oil word, which 'coating' wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A petronel was a large carbine or horse pistol of the 16th and 17th centuries, fired by cavalry with the butt braced against the chest.

clue.text: Transformed dress given a going over, in service

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the service

parts.note: the Royal Navy, one of the armed services

indicators.note: going over turns a thing over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a robe is a dress or gown

explanation.surface: A uniform, inspected thoroughly, is changed for military duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reborn has been spiritually renewed, made a new person, so the word means changed utterly.

clue.text: Lease king attached to form of estate I ignored

indicators.note: ignoring a letter leaves it out, so the I is dropped

parts.note: R is Rex, king
an entail is an estate settled on a fixed line of heirs

explanation.surface: A monarch's tenancy agreement for an estate where someone has been left out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is an arrangement to hire property for payment, the same contract as a lease.

clue.text: UK's No. 1 in Open struggling, only just in the lead? (5, two words)

indicators.note: in sets the first letter inside the other word
struggling suggests twisting about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
the first letter of UK

explanation.surface: Britain's top golfer, battling in the Open, holds a narrow lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open is golf's British Open championship.
explanation.definitionFit: One up is a golf score meaning ahead by a single hole, a slim advantage.

clue.text: Feature of requiem to fade with soaring swell within? (8, two words)

indicators.note: within places the reversed word inside the first one

parts.note: to die away is to fade

indicators.note: in a down entry, soaring rises upward, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to arise is to swell up

explanation.surface: A requiem's music dies away, then swells up again.
explanation.walkthrough: DI + ESIRA + E. Dies irae, 'day of wrath', is the Latin hymn sung in the requiem mass.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dies Irae is a sequence forming part of the Latin requiem mass, a standard section of it.

clue.text: A bandage applied to very large place? Discernment required

indicators.note: the bandage is put onto the following place, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: per means a, as in so much per head
a spica is a spiral bandage with overlapping turns, often applied to a limb
a city is a very large town

explanation.surface: Someone bandages an entire city, and is asked for discernment.
explanation.walkthrough: A spica is a figure-of-eight bandage, a word mostly met in Chambers; per stands for 'a' as in pounds per hour.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspicacity is keen mental insight, the quality of seeing clearly into things, which is discernment.

clue.text: Starmer's born afresh, producing strong campaign performances?

indicators.note: doing something afresh makes it anew, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: all the letters of both words

explanation.surface: Keir Starmer, Labour leader, reborn and giving rousing speeches on the trail.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnstormers were travelling actors and, later, politicians making vigorous tours of rural areas.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnstormer campaigns with flamboyant energy, so such people give vigorous electioneering displays; the noun phrase names them.

clue.text: Like e.g. US soldiers on parade, from Weald, leaderless, might one assume?

definitions.text: Like e.g. US soldiers on parade

wordplay.words: from Weald, leaderless, might one assume?
wordplay.note: Weald minus its first letter leaves four letters; the answer split into words is a recipe for building them, one pair placed inside another

explanation.surface: Soldiers drilling on a parade ground might be taken to be from an English county district.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, split AL IN ED, is the recipe that makes wEALD minus its leader. ALINED is a Chambers spelling of aligned, and 'US' flags GIs as American.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers on parade stand in straight rows, set in line, which is what aligned describes.

clue.text: Precise pointer at top of compass?

parts.note: N, north, is at the top of a compass
an arrow points the way

explanation.surface: A needle pointing exactly north on a compass dial.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow definition is exact and restricted, so narrow can mean strict or precise.

clue.text: Shelf honey industrious insect's found in

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the insect goes within the honey word

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, used in pharmacy
the ant is proverbially hard-working

explanation.surface: An ant has been found in honey on the shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantel is the shelf above a fireplace, a mantelpiece.

clue.text: Poison swallowed direct, dad dropped

indicators.note: the letters of dad are dropped from the joined words

parts.note: drank means swallowed
to lead is to direct
the letters D, A, D are taken as written

explanation.surface: A father's poisoning: he swallowed it as instructed and dropped dead.
explanation.walkthrough: From DRANKLEAD, D, A and D are 'dropped' one by one: the first D, the A of LEAD and the final D.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to fester and embitter, the sense in which a grievance poisons the mind.

clue.text: Avian spur son observed on magpies

parts.note: s abbreviates son
Pica is the magpie genus

explanation.surface: A bird's spur noticed on magpies by a boy.
explanation.definitionFit: In ornithology a spica is a spur, the horny spike on the leg of some birds.

clue.text: United in small island group, they're not wholly divine

indicators.note: in puts the single letter inside the word for islands

parts.note: aits are small river islands
U abbreviates United

explanation.surface: A set of islands united by beings who aren't quite gods.
explanation.definitionFit: An aitu is a Polynesian demigod, a being only partly divine.

clue.text: Crude fleece wrapped round in turn as a blanket

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, so the letters read right to left
a thing wrapped in other words is enclosed by them, so the letters lie within

parts.note: the letters run from the end of turn into blanket

explanation.surface: A rough sheepskin wrapped round someone as a blanket.
explanation.walkthrough: BASAN is sheepskin tanned in bark, an untreated, rough leather.
explanation.definitionFit: Basan is undressed sheepskin leather, a rough treated hide from a sheep.

clue.text: Check up about sign of what's not right in Paddy's bit of casual work

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads from bottom to top

a cross marks a wrong answer

explanation.walkthrough: Paddy signals an Irish word: a nixer is a job done on the side, often cash in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: In Irish English a nixer is a spare-time job outside regular employment, an odd job.

clue.text: Butterfly to free following rulebook

explanation.surface: Releasing a butterfly according to the regulations.

clue.text: Sandwiches: number in foreign bread set before one

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the bread word

parts.note: pain is French for bread
n stands for a number
Roman one

explanation.definitionFit: Panini are Italian toasted filled rolls, a kind of sandwich, and the word is plural.

clue.text: Pair reduced to single in travelling interrail, moving slowly?

a pair becoming a single means one of two matching letters goes

explanation.surface: Backpackers on an Interrail ticket, down to one of a couple, dawdle along.

clue.text: Large tropical fish, American, revealing soft metallic element

parts.note: the cero is a big mackerel of warm Atlantic waters
US abbreviates American

explanation.surface: A big tropical fish from America gives away a metal.

clue.text: Countryman's handle to lift on end of scythe

parts.note: to lift is to steal

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of scythe

explanation.surface: A farmhand grips the handle to raise his scythe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Countryman's' marks a dialect word: a steale is a handle, as of a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: In dialect a steale or stale is the long handle or shaft of a rake or similar tool.

clue.text: Acreage yokel yurned over for cows out of service

parts.note: a abbreviates acreage

indicators.note: the printed yurned is a slip for turned; turned over means flipped, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a swad is a country bumpkin

explanation.surface: A rustic turns his acres back to grazing cattle no longer used.
explanation.walkthrough: The source prints 'yurned', a typo for 'turned'. 'Out of service' marks an obsolete word: Spenser's adaw meant to daunt or subdue.
explanation.definitionFit: To adaw was to subdue or daunt, which is what cowing someone does; the word has long fallen out of use.

clue.text: One escaping mockery

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a sneer or jeer

explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated words share the spelling: one who flees, and a mocking look or remark.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleer works as a noun for a person running away and, separately, as a noun for a scornful grin.
